ANNmA ANNEX B

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Rotating Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. This standard has been prepared with a view to separately covering three-phase induction motors for USC in Nuclear Power Plants. The general requirements of three-phase induction motors are covered in IS 325 : 1996 `Specification for threcphase induction motors (jjlh revision )`. To ensure satisfactory installation and maintenance of induction motors, it is urged that the recommendations contained in IS 900 : 1992 `Code of practice for installation and maintenance of induction motors ( second revision )' should be carefully followed. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, obscrvcd or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Kules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard THREE-PHASE INDUCTION MOTORS FOR USE IN NUCLEAR POWER PLANTS - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE

4.1 Altitude and Temperature Motors shall be designed for the following site conditions unless otherwise agreed between the supplier and the purchaser. 4.1.1 Altitude Altitude not exceeding 1000 m. Motors intended for service on sites where the altitude is in excess of
1000 mare covered by 4.1.1 of IS 325. 4.1.2 Temperature

1.1 This standard covers three-phase induction motors for voltages up to and including 11 000 volts having windings with Class B, Class F and Class C insulation ( see IS 127 1 ) for use in Nuclear Power Plants. The motors specified in this standard are assigned any one of the ratings specified in 9.4. 1.2 Motors within the scope of this standard for use on systems employing non-preferred voltages and frequencies shall be considered as complying with this standard provided that they comply in all other respects with this standard. The voltages and frequency for which they are designed shall be stated on the rating plate. 1.3 In addition to this standard, the motor shall comply with IS 325 in cases where no specific requirement is given in this standard. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The list of Indian Standards given in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3TERMlNOLoGY 3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions in addition to those given in IS 1885 ( Part 35 )/IEC 50 ( 4 11 >shall apply. 3.1 Full Load The state of a motor rotating at normal speed under rated conditions when rated output is required of it. 3.2 Overload Any load in excess of the rated load, usually expressed numerically as the amount percentage excess torque for motors. 3.2.1 Sustained Overload An overload sustained for a sufficiently long period to affect appreciably the temperature of the motor. 3.2.2 Momentary Overload An overload the duration of which is so short as not to affect appreciably the tempcraturc of the motors. 4 SITE CONDITIONS 4.0 The following shall constitute the normal site conditions. 1

The reference ambient temperature for both LT and HT motors shall be 50�C. For motors having CACW cooling the reference water temperature shall be given in Annex B. 4.2 Humidity Unless otherwise specified, all motors shall be designed for operation in an ambient with a relative humidity 01 90 percent at 4O'C. 4.3 Radiations Where specified, motors shall be designed tocontinuously operate under a cumulative dose of lo* Rads of gama radiations. Such motors shall also be capable of continuous service after withstanding building pressure test, during which the pressure of air seen by the motor will be 1.5 kg/cm2 (gauge). The capability of the motor to withstand air pressure of 1.5 kg/cm* may be proved either by calculations or by any other method agreed between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.4 Motors which are to be installed in the reactor building must be capable of withstanding pressure and temperature transients steam environment, which may occur on account of LOCA (Loss of Coolant Accident) condition when the areas in the reactor building where motors are installed may become steam bound for a short duration as indicated in Annex B. The temperature of steam and pressure seen by motor inside reactor building in case of accident shall bc given in Annex B. Test methods shall be mutually agreed between the manufacturers and the customers. 4.5 Form and Symmetry of Cumnts and Voltages 4.5.1 In the cast of thcsc motors, the supply voltage is assumed to be virtually sinusoidal as

IS 14578 : 1999 defined below: The voltage is considered to be virtually sinusoidal, if, when supplying an ac motor at rated load, the waveform is such that the difference between the instantaneous value and value of the limdamental component does not exceed five percent of the amplitude of the latter. In temperature-rise testing, such amplitude difference shall not exceed 2.5 percent. 4.5.2 These motors shall also be capable of operation with an unbalance of 3 percent in supply voltage when calculated as per IS 13529. Should the limits at 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 occur simulmneot@~ in service at the rated load, this shall not lead to any deleterious temperature in the motor and it is recommended that the excess resulting temperaturerise shall not be more than 10�Cthan the value specified in Table 1 of IS 12802. In temperature-rise testing, the negative sequence component shall be less than 0.5 percent of the positive sequence component of the system of voltages, the influence of the zero-sequence component being eliminated. By agreement between the supplier and the purchaser, the negative-sequence component of the system of currents may be measured instead of the negative sequence component of the voltages, and this shall not exceed 2.5 percent oftbe positive-sequence component of the system of currents. 4.6 Supply Voltage and Frequency Variation Unless otherwise specified, all motors shall be capable of delivering the rated output under following variation in supply voltage and frequency: a) Variation in voltage from its rated value f 10 percent, b) Variation in frequency A 5 percent, and c) Combined variation in voltage and frequency l 10 percent. In case of continuous operation at extreme voltage limits, the temperature-rise limits specified in 13 shall not exceed by more than 5�C. Motors when operated under the extreme conditions of voltage and frequency variation may not necessarily have their performance in accordance with this standard. 4.7 Whenever specified the motors shall be designed either for SSE ( Safe Shut Down Earthquake ) or for OBE ( Operation Basis Earthquake ) to meet the floor response spectra applicable or to meet the coda1 requirement depending on the seismic zone, as per IS 1893. However, the method of qualification shall be subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier.

5 TYPES OF ENCLOSURES 5.1 Motors covered by this standard shall have one of the degrees of protection in accordance with IS 469 1.
6 METHOD OF COOLING

6.1 The methods of cooling of motors and their
designations shall be in accordance with IS 6362/ IEC Pub 34-6-1991. 7 MATERLALS 7.1 All materials and components used in the manufacture of motors shall conform to relevant Indian Standards wherever these exist. Whenever it is not practicable to comply with this requirement, it shall be subject to agreement between the supplier and the purchaser. 7.2 For motors of 3 300 V and above, the windings, coils and insulation system shall be capable of withstanding an impulse of 1.2150 micro set at Up ( = 4Un + 5 ) kV, where Un is the line voltage. The insulation system for the motors shall also be suitable to withstand satisfactorily the voltage surges produced due to chopping of currents by vacuum circuit breakers controlling the motors without any deterioration when surge suppressors are not provided. The supplier may carry out necessary tests on sample coils in accordance with IS 14222 to prove this capability. 7.3 When radiation withstand level is specified, the motor windings and all the components ofthe insulation system shall be suitable to withstand the maximum expected value of the cumulative dose of 10s Rads of gama radiations. Also for motors located in radiation area, the materials used for the parts designed for periodic replacement ( such as seals, gaskets, `0' rings, etc ) the period of unimpaired operation with respect to radiation damage shall be at least 5 years. In case such materials are not capable of withstanding such radiations, the replacement programme shall be clearly stated. 7.4 The slot wedges in large machines shall preferably be of non-magnetic material. 7.5 The retaining rings if used for the rotor shall be of non-magnetic forged material. 7.6 Painting
.

7.6.1 The motor external parts shall be finished and painted to produce a neat and durable surface which would prevent rusting and corrosion. The equipment shall be thoroughly degreased, all rust, sharp edges and scale removed and treated with one coat of primer and finished with two coats of enamel paint to shade 631ofIS5.

IS 14578 : 1999 7.6.2 For the motors in the reactor building, the painting shall be done with epoxy based paint system. 8 SPACE HEATERS g.1 The motors rated 30 kW and above shall be provided with space heaters of adequate capacity to maintain motor internal temperature above the dew point, to prevent moisture condensation, when the motor is not in service. The space heaters shall be located at the accessible places in the lower part of the motor. 8.2 For motors of less than 30 kW, it shall be possible to connect 24 V ac supply to stator winding for space heating when the motor is not in service. 9 PREFERRED VOLTAGES, FREQUENCY AND OUTPUT 9.1 Preferred Voltages For the purpose of this standard, the preferred voltages shall be in accordance with IS 12360. The voltages preferred for three-phase, 50 Hz machines are : 415V 3.3kV, 6.6kVand 1lkV 10 DIMENSIONS 10.1 The dimensions of foot-mounted induction motors and flange mounted induction motors shall preferably be in accordance with IS 123 1 and IS 2223 respectively.
NOTES 1 The relationship between output and frame sizes shall preferably be as specified in IS 1231 and IS 2223 for general purpose application for foot-mounted induction motors and flange mounted induction motors respectively. 2 The dimensions and output ratings for foot-mounted electrical machines with frame numbers 355 to 1 080 are given in IS 8223.

11 DUTY AND RATING 11.1 The class of duty ratings assigned to motors has been specified in 9 of IS 325. The class of duty of the motor shall be agreed between the supplier and the purchaser. 11.2 Starting Duty 11.2.1 The general purpose motors for driving fans or pumps whose GD2 values referred to motor speed are the same or lower than motor GD2 shall be capable of two successive restarts when coupled to its driven equipment, with coasting down to rest between starts under both cold and hot conditions and a third restart shall be feasible after 20 min. The motor shall further be capable of three equally time spaced starts in an hour, the motor initially being at a temperature, not exceeding the rated load operating temperature. 11.2.2 For other applications, the starting duty shall be as agreed between the purchaser and the supplier. 11.3 Fast Bus-Transfer The motors shall be capable of withstanding the voltage torque stresses developed due to the vector difference between the residual voltage and the incoming supply voltage equal to 150percent motor rated voltage during fast changeover of the supply. 12 EARTHING 12.1 Earthing of the motor shall be done in accordance with the relevant provisions of IS 3043. 13 TEMPERATURkXISE 13.1 The limits of permissible temperature-rise of windings with Class B and Class F insulation shall be in accordance with Table 1 of IS 12802. For Class C insulation, the permissible temperature-rise shall be as agreed between the purchaser and the supplier. 13.2 Under normal conditions of use, the motors rated up to 650 V and located in the reactor building and also all motors rated above 1 100 V shall have windings 3

Unless otherwise specified the maximum permissible noise level shall be as specified in IS 12065. 17 PERFORMANCE VALUES The performance values of the motor for use in Nuclear Power Plant shall be governed in accordance with IS 325. 18 EFFICIENCY AND POWER FACTOR The provisions of 17 of IS 325 shall apply.
19 TOLERANCE

22.1 The general information to be furnished when inquiring for and ordering an electrical motor is given in Annex B 23 TESTS 23.1 The provision of 22 to 27 of IS 325 shall be applicable. 23.2 The following tests may be performed when specified and agreed between the supplier and the purchaser: a) Vibration test as per IS 12075, b) Overspeed test, c) Tan delta and delta tan delta test on winding ( only for motors rated above 3 kV. ), d) Polarization index test ( for HT motors only ), and e) Shaft voltage measurement.
NOTE reference The tests at (c), (d) and (e) above shall be for only.

Unless otherwise specified, tolerances applicable to the determined values shall be in accordance with Table 1 of IS 325. 20 TERMINAL MARRING Terminal markings when used shall be in accordance with IS 4728. 21 MARRING 21.1 A rating plate stating the following shall be supplied with each motor:

a) Reference to this standard, that is, Ref ISS. b) Induction motor;

23.3 The methods of test shall be in accordance with IS 4029. 24 SEISMIC TESTS Whenever specified by the purchaser at the time of the enquiry and specifically agreed to by the supplier while commenting on the specification, the supplier shall prove either by actual testing or by design calculations that seismic accelerations of specified magnitude will not affect the life of bearings, change in air gap length or cause any structural failure, and motor will continue to run even after the earthquake, without any deterioration in performance. 4

ANNEX B (CZauses4.1.2,4.4and22.1 )

INFORMATION To BE GlVEN WITH ENQUIRY ANB ORDER When inquiring for and ordering an electrical motor to comply with this standard the following particulars should be supplied: 1) Site and operating conditions; 2) Reference to this standard, that is, Ref ISS ....*......... 3) Type of enclosure; 4) Class of duty; 5) Method of cooling; 20) Particulars of tests required and where they are to be carried out; 21) Particulars as to whether voltage-limiting devices will be employed; 22) Rotor, whether squirrel cage or slip-ring; 23) Details of shaft extension required; 24) `Ijpe of slip-ring gear, whether continuously rated or for starting purposes only, and whether to be fitted with brush lifting or shortcircuiting arrangements or both, and if interlocks are required; 25) Method of starting to be employed; 26) Breakaway torque in terms of the rated-load torque and the corresponding breakaway starting current which may be taken from the supply with the starting apparatus in circuit; 27) Nature of load and any information regarding the driven machine which has a bearing upon the torque required during the accelerating period, the kinetic energy of the moving parts to be accelerated, and the number of starts during a specified period; 28) For high voltage motors, system fault level and duration of the fault along with the details of protective devices and cable of the system to which the motor is connected to enable the manufacturer to design a suitable terminal box; 29) Method of drive; 30) Temperature of steam and pressure in Reactor building under LOCA condition and maximum duration of steam exposure; 31) Seismic requirements; and 32) Any specific requirement. Attention is directed to the duty rating of switching starter as specified in IS 13947 ( Part 4/Set 1).
